input.quote: Risk of loss for all Base Components shall at all times remain with IBM. Risk of loss for all Customer Components shall at all times remain with Customer.
input.rationale: A full-text search for "insurance" returns no results and the outline contains no insurance heading, so the agreement imposes no coverage obligation on IBM. IBM is a hosting vendor that operates the e-business Hosting Environment and holds Customer Components/Customer Data (§ 5.3), which is exactly the profile the rule targets; absence of any insurance for a vendor processing our data is walk-away territory. We inserted the playbook's preferred coverage (CGL USD 1M/2M, E&O USD 2M, cyber USD 5M, workers' compensation, certificates on request) as a new § 14.12A immediately after Risk of Loss in the miscellaneous section, flagging the E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M fallback as a negotiating position.

proposal.summary: Insert a vendor insurance clause in Section 14 (after Risk of Loss)
proposal.comment: [Playbook] The agreement has no insurance provision even though IBM hosts and processes our data, so we have added our standard coverage requirements (CGL USD 1M/2M, E&O USD 2M, cyber USD 5M) with certificates on request. If helpful, we can accept E&O of USD 1M and cyber of USD 2M as a fallback.

ops.text: IBM shall maintain, at its own expense, throughout the term and for one (1) year thereafter: commercial general liability insurance of not less than USD 1,000,000 per occurrence and USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate; professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000; cyber and privacy liability insurance of not less than USD 5,000,000; and workers' compensation insurance as required by law. IBM shall provide certificates of insurance to Customer on request.
